title: Cohorted LTS Strategy: Compatibility Matrix Across Runtime/API/SDK/Console + Automated Rollout Validators
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: As we expand LTS cohorts (stability lanes) across runtime, hosted API, client SDKs, and Console, we lack a single canonical compatibility matrix and automated preflight validators that can gate cross-surface rollouts. This leads to partial deployments, unexpected client breakage, and manual coordination overhead for upgrades.

Proposal summary: Deliver a cohorted LTS compatibility matrix (CSV + dashboard) and an automated Rollout Validator service. The matrix maps supported pairings for: runtime binary versions, hosted API contract versions, SDK major/minor compatibility, and Console feature flags. The Rollout Validator runs preflight checks (integration smoke tests, API contract checks, byte-compat checks for SDKs, migration script verification, telemetry SLO sanity) and exposes a pass/fail signal to our rollout system (canary gates, workforce alerts, and automatic rollback).

Scope (MVP): 1) Define matrix schema and produce compatibility CSV for runtime, API, SDKs, Console. 2) Implement validator runners for: API contract tests (OpenAPI diff + contract suites), SDK compatibility tests (consumer test harness against pinned runtime/API), basic migration-runner for DB/schema-affecting changes, and KV/cache prewarming validation. 3) Integrate validator outputs into rollout automation (staged canaries, percent-based promotion, immediate rollback on validator-fail). 4) Instrument telemetry and create a Console dashboard for matrix and gate status.

Out of scope: Full per-customer private deployment orchestration (that will be follow-up), advanced binary-level rollback automation, and language-specific SDKs beyond our top-3 (Python, TypeScript, Go) for MVP.

Why now: Increasing frequency of runtime and API updates plus enterprise customers requesting LTS guarantees. Without a formal matrix and automated validators, upgrades require heavy manual coordination and increase risk of regressions and outages.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical compatibility matrix published and stored in repo (CSV + human-readable MD) describing supported pairings across runtime, API, SDKs, Console for LTS cohorts.
Rollout Validator service implemented that can run a configurable preflight suite and return structured pass/fail reasons.
Integration: rollout automation consumes validator result and stops/promotes canaries based on policy (50%, 90%, 100% thresholds) with documented rollback path.
Three SDK compatibility test harnesses (Python, TypeScript, Go) implemented and run in CI against the runtime and API matrix entries.
Console dashboard page shows current matrix, active rollouts, and last-validator results; accessible to PMs and oncall.
Runbook updated: upgrade playbooks include validation step, escalation path, and post-upgrade verification checklist.
notes: Matrix schema fields: component, semantic_version, cohort (lts-stable|lts-sustained|stable), supported_clients (list), min_api_version, max_api_version, required_console_flags, notes

Validator types: openapi-diff (detect breaking contract changes), smoke (end-to-end happy-path), perf-sanity (latency p95 within X% of baseline), kv-prewarm check, migration-simulation (dry-run), sdk-under-test integration.
Policy suggestion: allow runtime minor bumps within same cohort without requiring SDK bumps if API contract unchanged; require explicit matrix entry for any cross-cohort compatibility promise.
Risk: false-positive validator failures can block urgent security releases — add bypass gated to SRE lead with audit logging.
Telemetry: add metrics for validator_pass_rate, time_to_unblock, rollback_count_by_release, customer_errors_post_upgrade.
Related artifacts: design doc in Confluence, initial CSV in repo, prototype validator runner in tools/rollout/validators.
Owner: Release Engineering (Miguel) accountable; Runtime team to publish compatibility metadata on build; SDK leads to maintain compatibility tests.
